subject: fix(table/dv): read deletion vectors by content_offset when the file is not a Puffin container (#2071)
body:
* fix(table/dv): read deletion vectors by content_offset when the file is not a Puffin container

Databricks writes deletion vectors for IcebergCompatV3 (UniForm) tables as a
Delta deletion_vector_*.bin file: a one-byte version prefix followed by
deletion-vector-v1 blobs, with no Puffin header or footer. The manifest entry
is well-formed (file_format=PUFFIN, referenced_data_file, content_offset,
content_size_in_bytes point at a valid blob), and the Java reference reader
(BaseDeleteLoader.readDV) reads such files because it never consults the
Puffin footer: it reads content_size_in_bytes bytes at content_offset.

ReadDV/ReadDVs opened the file with puffin.NewReader first and failed with
"puffin: invalid header magic" on these tables.

- puffin: NewReader wraps the header-magic and too-small errors in a new
  sentinel, ErrNotPuffinFile, so callers can detect "no Puffin container".
- table/dv: when the DV file is not a Puffin container, fall back to reading
  the blobs directly at content_offset (Java parity). The blob's length,
  magic and CRC-32 are still verified by DeserializeDV and the decoded
  cardinality is validated against the manifest record_count; footer-only
  checks (blob type, referenced-data-file property, cardinality property)
  are skipped with a slog warning. Real Puffin files keep the existing
  strict path unchanged.

Verified against a Databricks Unity Catalog IcebergCompatV3 table read through
the UC Iceberg REST catalog with vended credentials: 968,980 rows after
1,020 deletes + 1,020 updates, matching the SQL result; copy-on-write and
non-DV tables unaffected.

Fixes #2070

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MqCR5xLuYcb7Baw6Xbj4be

* fix(table/dv): scope ErrNotPuffinFile to magic-first, reuse the open handle for bare DV reads

Review follow-up:

- puffin.NewReader checks the header magic before the minimum-size guard.
  ErrNotPuffinFile is returned only when the file is too short to hold the
  magic or the leading bytes are not PFA1; a file that starts with the magic
  but is truncated keeps the plain "puffin: file too small" error, so a
  partial upload of a real Puffin file is never routed to the bare-blob path.
- openDVReader returns the still-open file (nil reader) on ErrNotPuffinFile;
  readBareDVs reads from that handle instead of reopening the path.
- readBareDVs no longer re-runs validateDVFile (both callers validate before
  dispatch; documented), reads blobs in content_offset order and restores
  input order, and logs the "not a Puffin container" warning once per file
  path, after the first blob decoded.
- Tests: truncated / corrupt-footer Puffin files fail without wrapping
  ErrNotPuffinFile; bare blob with corrupt CRC surfaces the "blob at offset"
  wrap; reversed-offset input keeps output order; puffin size test uses a
  valid-magic short file plus a too-short-for-magic case.

Re-verified against a fresh Databricks IcebergCompatV3 table with two
deletion vectors: 999,000 rows / 1,000 updated markers, matching SQL.

subject: feat(catalog/glue): support Amazon S3 Tables federated catalogs (#2001)
body:
* feat(catalog/glue): support Amazon S3 Tables federated catalogs

Tables in a Glue database federated to Amazon S3 Tables (ConnectionType
aws:s3tables) could not be created through the Glue catalog: the service
assigns storage itself, so the generic client-side location resolution
fails with "no default path set".

Detect the federated database and create such tables in two phases,
mirroring pyiceberg: create a minimal Glue entry so S3 Tables allocates
storage, read the assigned location, write Iceberg metadata to it, then
repoint the Glue entry. The allocated entry is rolled back on any later
failure. An explicit location is rejected for these tables, and a missing
version id is treated as a failed commit.

S3 Tables entries also report a service-specific Glue TableType (e.g.
"customer"), so getRawTable now accepts any entry marked as Iceberg via
the table_type parameter, not only EXTERNAL_TABLE.

Adds unit coverage for detection, the two-phase create, location
rejection, every rollback path, and the relaxed TableType gate, plus a
gated live integration test.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* fix(catalog/glue): don't roll back S3 Tables table on reload failure

The final LoadTable ran inside the create's rollback scope, so a
transient read failure after a successful commit deleted an
already-created table (and reclaimed its storage). Move the reload out
of that scope: only allocate/write/commit failures roll back now, which
also matches the generic create path. Document that S3 Tables keeps its
own Glue TableType on the commit update.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* test(catalog/glue): reload a service TableType in the S3 Tables create test

Have the successful create path's mocked reload return a service-specific
TableType ("customer"), so the happy path also exercises the relaxed
getRawTable gate rather than only EXTERNAL_TABLE.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* address review: lazy federation detection and scope getRawTable relaxation

- CreateTable now tries the generic path first and only probes for S3 Tables
  federation when location resolution fails with ErrNoDefaultLocation. This
  removes the redundant GetDatabase on default creates and avoids a new
  glue:GetDatabase requirement on explicit-location creates.
- Export internal.ErrNoDefaultLocation so the probe matches it via errors.Is
  instead of the error string.
- Scope the relaxed getRawTable TableType gate to entries actually federated
  to S3 Tables (Table.FederatedTable.ConnectionType == aws:s3tables), so
  non-federated databases keep their pre-existing behavior.
- Tests: prove explicit-location creates skip the probe, prove a non-federated
  iceberg-param table is still rejected, and update federated mocks.

* address review: reject explicit S3 Tables location, soften federation probe

- CreateTable rejects an explicit location for a federated S3 Tables
  database instead of silently creating a table outside managed storage.
- isS3TablesDatabase treats AccessDeniedException as not-federated so a
  caller lacking glue:GetDatabase still reaches the generic create path.
- Document the two residual create failures left to the service.
- Tighten the metadata-write-failure test to assert the write error.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* catalog/glue: best-effort clean up S3 Tables metadata on commit failure

When UpdateTable fails after WriteMetadata, the rollback now best-effort
deletes the written metadata object before dropping the minimal Glue entry.
For S3 Tables the managed location may be unreachable, so the removal error
is ignored and reclaiming any remainder is left to the service, as documented.
The existing UpdateTable-failure test now asserts the metadata file is gone.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* catalog/glue: make stranded S3 Tables entry droppable and harden the commit

- DropTable/getRawTable now accept a minimal federated S3 Tables entry
  (format=ICEBERG, no table_type), so a double-failure leftover is cleaned
  up through DropTable, restoring parity with pyiceberg's delete_table.
- The UpdateTable repoint preserves the service-assigned TableType instead
  of forcing EXTERNAL_TABLE, which S3 Tables rejects on write; a unit test
  now asserts the TableType we send.
- The rollback DeleteTable runs on a context detached from a cancelled
  create (context.WithoutCancel + timeout) and joins errors with errors.Join.
- isS3TablesDatabase guards against a nil Database from getDatabase.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* catalog/glue: keep the live-proven EXTERNAL_TABLE on the S3 Tables repoint

Sending the allocated entry's own TableType was untested against S3 Tables
and races the service's federation (nil right after CreateTable, "customer"
once federated). Live testing confirmed S3 Tables accepts EXTERNAL_TABLE on
the repoint, so send it unconditionally and assert it in the unit test.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* catalog/glue: note S3 Tables ignores the repoint TableType (verified live)

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* fix(catalog/glue): write table metadata with the catalog AWS config

The metadata writes in CreateTable, commitS3TablesTable, and CommitTable used
a bare context, so the S3 FileIO resolver fell back to LoadDefaultConfig. A
catalog built with WithAwsConfig or glue.* static credentials would then call
Glue as the configured principal but PUT metadata as the ambient one (or fail
despite valid configured credentials). Wrap the context with the catalog's AWS
config before each write, matching RegisterTable and convertGlueToIceberg; for
commitS3TablesTable this also covers the staged.FS metadata cleanup.

* test(catalog/glue): mock GetDatabase in TestGlueCreateTableAlreadyExists

Merging main brought in TestGlueCreateTableAlreadyExists, which does an
explicit-location create. CreateTable now consults the database up front to
reject federated S3 Tables locations, so the test must mock GetDatabase; a
non-federated result lets it take the generic path and assert the
AlreadyExists mapping. In real AWS a missing glue:GetDatabase surfaces as
AccessDenied, which isS3TablesDatabase already treats as non-federated.

* address review: resolve federation up front and harden S3 Tables create

- CreateTable now fetches the database once and decides S3 Tables federation for
  both default and explicit-location creates, reusing the result for namespace
  properties so staging issues no second GetDatabase. This also catches catalogs
  with a `warehouse` property, where the previous lazy probe let a federated
  create write outside the managed storage.
- Map AlreadyExistsException from the S3 Tables allocate step to
  catalog.ErrTableAlreadyExists, matching the other create paths.
- Reject RenameTable for federated S3 Tables tables, whose managed storage the
  copy-then-delete rename cannot safely repoint.
- Replace isS3TablesDatabase with lookupDatabase (AccessDenied/NotFound tolerant)
  and extract namespacePropsFromDatabase.

Tests: credential-boundary regression tests (memfs FileIO recording the ctx AWS
config) for CreateTable, commitS3TablesTable incl. the fs.Remove cleanup, and
CommitTable; warehouse-set federated create; allocate AlreadyExists; rename
rejection; catalog-id pinning; and AssertExpectations on the fall-through test.

* Trim comments

* Address review nits

---------

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

subject: fix(manifest): support nanosecond timestamp partitions (#2034)
body:
* fix(manifest): support nanosecond timestamp partition types in Avro schema

partitionTypeToAvroSchema had no arm for TimestampNsType or
TimestampTzNsType, so any v3 table partitioned on a timestamp_ns or
timestamptz_ns column fell through to "unsupported partition type" and
could not have a manifest written at all. NewManifestWriter calls
partitionTypeToAvroSchema before anything else, so the failure is
unconditional.

The read side already handles these types: the manifest decoder switches
on atype.TimestampNanos, and catalog/rest/scan_task_decoder.go maps both
ns types to atype.TimestampNanos. The library could read partitions it
could not write.

Add TimestampNsNode and TimestampTzNsNode to the internal Avro schema
nodes, using atype.TimestampNanos with adjust-to-utc false and true
respectively, mirroring the existing micros nodes, and wire both ns
types into the partition type switch.

Signed-off-by: Jeremy Schoemaker <jeremy@shoemoney.com>

subject: refactor(table)!: extract orphan cleanup into table/maintenance (#2086)
body:
* refactor(table)!: extract orphan cleanup into table/maintenance

This is Slice 1 of issue #2083, breaking pre-v1 relocation of the orphan cleanup
service from the table package into a dedicated table/maintenance package.

Changes:
- Create new table/maintenance package with Service facade
- Move DeleteOrphanFiles, PlanOrphanFiles, ExecuteOrphanCleanup, and PurgeFiles
  methods from table.Table to maintenance.Service
- Move exported types: OrphanCleanupOption, OrphanCleanupResult, OrphanCleanupPlan,
  OrphanFile, PrefixMismatchMode (and constants)
- Move helper functions: WithLocation, WithFilesOlderThan, WithDryRun,
  WithDeleteFunc, WithCleanupMaxConcurrency, WithPrefixMismatchMode,
  WithEqualSchemes, WithEqualAuthorities
- Export IsGCEnabled from table package (was unexported isGCEnabled)
- Update all callers in catalog/ and cmd/iceberg/ to use new API:
  maintenance.New(tbl).DeleteOrphanFiles(...) instead of tbl.DeleteOrphanFiles(...)
- Move tests to table/maintenance package
- Update IsGCEnabled references in transaction.go and updates.go

The new public entry shape maintains ergonomic parity with the original API.
To use orphan cleanup: create a maintenance service with maintenance.New(table),
then call its methods.

BREAKING: table.DeleteOrphanFiles, table.PlanOrphanFiles, table.ExecuteOrphanCleanup,
and table.PurgeFiles are no longer available on table.Table. Use table/maintenance
package instead.

* style(table): gofmt the moved orphan-cleanup test

table/maintenance/orphan_cleanup_test.go was not gofmt-clean after the move (a
block comment needed re-indentation), which failed the golangci-lint gofmt check
in CI. Formatting only, no behavior change.

* refactor(table/maintenance): use free functions and restore dropped tests

Address review feedback on the orphan-cleanup extraction:

- Replace the Service facade with free functions that take the table as their
  first argument (maintenance.DeleteOrphanFiles(ctx, tbl, ...)), matching
  table/compaction, and update all callers in catalog/ and cmd/iceberg/. This
  avoids freezing a stateful constructor at v1; a deprecation shim on
  table.Table is impossible anyway because table/maintenance imports table.
- Rename the four generic options to the WithCleanup* prefix
  (WithCleanupLocation/DryRun/DeleteFunc/FilesOlderThan) for consistency with
  WithCleanupMaxConcurrency before the names freeze.
- Restore the tests and benchmarks dropped in the move: the statistics- and
  tombstone-reference tests, the manifest-dedup and concurrency-limit tests,
  the negative-/zero-age retention checks, and the PurgeFiles and manifest-list
  benchmarks, porting their shared IO and manifest helpers into the package.
- Document table.IsGCEnabled's parsing rules now that it is exported, and add a
  package doc comment.
- Fix website/src/api.md and releases.md (with a moved-symbols compatibility
  note), and add a `make vet` target running `go vet -tags=integration ./...`
  (wired into CI) so the moved //go:build integration test stays compiled.

* docs(table/maintenance): document OrphanCleanupOption and the WithCleanup* options

Add one-line doc comments with defaults to OrphanCleanupOption,
WithCleanupLocation (table data location), WithCleanupFilesOlderThan (72h),
and WithCleanupDryRun (false), now that the WithCleanup* names are fixed for v1.

subject: feat(table): add tunables to bound compaction pipeline memory (#1993)
body:
* Add tunables bounding compaction pipeline memory

The compaction read+write pipeline had fixed memory characteristics:
the scanner decodes read.parquet.batch-size rows per Arrow batch
(131072 by default) with no per-scan override, and each rolling data
writer buffers up to 64 record batches in its input channel with no way
to lower or raise that bound. On wide rows the product of those two
numbers dominates a compaction worker's peak memory.

- WithArrowBatchSize scan option caps the rows decoded per Arrow batch
  for one scan, overriding the table's read.parquet.batch-size without
  mutating caller-supplied scan options.
- The rolling data writers' record channel capacity (default 64
  batches) is now configurable via the WithRecordBatchBufferSize write
  option, threaded through recordWritingArgs to the writer factory. It
  applies to both the fanout and the clustered write paths, which share
  the rolling writer.
- WithParquetRowGroupLimit write option overrides the table's
  write.parquet.row-group-limit per write, bounding rows buffered per
  row group before each flush.
- Compaction group options forward all three into
  ExecuteCompactionGroup: WithCompactionReadBatchSize,
  WithCompactionRecordBatchBufferSize, and
  WithCompactionParquetRowGroupLimit.

Signed-off-by: KranzL <50032317+KranzL@users.noreply.github.com>

subject: fix(catalog/rest): don't bind the cached vended-credential FileIO to the caller's context (#2079)
body:
* fix(catalog/rest): don't bind the cached vended-credential FileIO to the caller's context

vendedCredentialRefresher.loadFS caches the FileIO it builds and hands it
to every later caller, but built it with the first caller's ctx. The GCS
filesystem keeps the context it is opened with, so once that ctx was
cancelled every later operation through the table failed with
context.Canceled, even when called with a live context. Any writer that
scopes each commit to its own context (e.g. context.WithTimeout) saw
every commit after the first fail. Renewal had the same issue, and so
did prefixScopedIO, which stores the ctx and opens filesystems lazily.

Build the cached IO from context.WithoutCancel(ctx): values are kept,
cancellation is not. fetchCreds still honours ctx.

Fixes #2078

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Stephane Loeuillet <stephane.loeuillet@kaiko.com>

* fix(catalog/rest): let the refresher own the vended FileIO's lifetime

Review follow-up. Detaching the cached IO from the caller's cancellation
left close() as the only teardown, and renewal replaced the cached IO
without closing it, so a superseded IO's background work leaked.

The refresher now opens the IO on its own cancellable context, derived
from context.WithoutCancel(ctx). Renewal installs the new IO, then closes
the superseded one and cancels its context; a failed renewal cancels only
the context it created and keeps the cached IO. close() closes the IO and
cancels its context.

newPrefixScopedIO keeps the context it is given (documented): that is how
close reaches the filesystems it opens lazily.

Tests: renewal is asserted to rebuild the IO on a distinct context, keep
values, and retire the old IO; close and a failed renewal are covered;
first-caller value inheritance is documented rather than promised; checked
type assertion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Stephane Loeuillet <stephane.loeuillet@kaiko.com>

* fix(catalog/rest): keep the superseded vended FileIO usable on renewal

Review follow-up. Closing and cancelling the superseded IO on renewal
broke callers still holding it (manifest planning batches, partial
rewrites, concurrent scans and writes on derived tables), and the leak it
guarded against does not exist for the gocloud backends. replaceIO is
swap-only again; close() still closes the current IO and cancels its
context.

Tests now run on a real blobfs.FileIO over memblob, opened on the
context it is given: the cached IO is used after the first caller's
cancellation, and the IO from before a renewal is used after it (this
fails with "blob: Bucket has been closed" on the previous commit). The
NotSame check, which tested the context's implementation rather than the
renewal, is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Stephane Loeuillet <stephane.loeuillet@kaiko.com>

* fix(catalog/rest): document why the vended IO keeps ctx values; drop unused test field

Review nits: the S3 factory reads its base AWS config from the context values WithoutCancel keeps, so say so next to it; contextCapturingScheme.scheme was never read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Stephane Loeuillet <stephane.loeuillet@kaiko.com>

* docs(catalog/rest): say why replaceIO drops the superseded cancel

subject: fix(catalog/rest): sign SigV4 with credentials from catalog properties (#1999)
body:
* fix(catalog/rest): sign SigV4 with credentials from catalog properties

The REST catalog's SigV4 signer only used the AWS default credential chain
(config.LoadDefaultConfig), ignoring the s3.* credential properties passed to
the catalog. This forced callers targeting AWS SigV4 REST catalogs (S3 Tables,
Glue) to export AWS_* environment variables even when they supplied credentials
via catalog properties.

Build a static credentials provider from s3.access-key-id / s3.secret-access-key
/ s3.session-token when present, and only fall back to the default chain
otherwise. An explicitly provided aws.Config (WithAwsConfig) still wins.

This mirrors the same gap tracked for the Python client in
apache/iceberg-python#2070.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* test(catalog/rest): pin SigV4 props-cred signing; error on partial creds

Address review feedback:
- Add TestSigV4SignsWithPropsCredentials, which asserts the SigV4 Authorization
  header is signed with the credentials from catalog properties. This pins the
  wiring: removing the cfg.Credentials assignment makes the test fail.
- staticCredsFromProps now returns an error when only one of the access-key /
  secret-access-key pair is set, instead of silently falling back to the ambient
  default identity. Neither set still falls back to the default chain.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* docs(catalog/rest): document SigV4 signing credential precedence

Address review feedback (minor): the SigV4 signing identity resolves as
WithAwsConfig > s3.* catalog properties > AWS default credential chain. Document
this on WithSigV4 and in the rest.sigv4-enabled configuration reference.

Signed-off-by: iremcaginyurtturk <cagin.yurtturk@getbruin.com>

* fix(catalog/rest): error on incomplete SigV4 creds via ValidateStaticCredentials

Delegate staticCredsFromProps to internal/awsconfig.ValidateStaticCredentials so
a token-only s3.session-token (no access/secret key) returns the
ErrIncompleteStaticCredentials sentinel instead of silently dropping to the
default credential chain. Add a token-only test case and assert the sentinel via
errors.Is. Document the s3.* vs Java rest.* divergence in the WithSigV4 godoc and
configuration.md.

* feat(catalog/rest): accept Java rest.* SigV4 credential aliases

Accept rest.access-key-id / rest.secret-access-key / rest.session-token as
aliases for the s3.* signing-credential properties, resolved per field with the
s3.* keys taking precedence. This lets operators migrating from the Java client
configure SigV4 signing with the property names they already use instead of
silently falling through to the AWS default credential chain.

* fix(catalog/rest): harden SigV4 credential boundaries

Two credential-boundary fixes for the props-based SigV4 signing path:

- Resolve the credential tuple atomically per namespace. Resolving each field
  independently let a partial s3.* pair be completed with a rest.* field (or
  inherit an unrelated rest.* token), signing as a hybrid identity that still
  passed validation. Now if any s3.* field is set we validate and use only the
  s3.* tuple, otherwise only the rest.* tuple; never backfill across namespaces.

- Do not re-sign a cross-origin redirect. sessionTransport signed every hop, so
  a redirect to a different origin exposed the SigV4 Authorization header and
  session token to an unconfigured host. Signing is now skipped when the request
  origin (scheme/host/effective port) differs from the configured catalog origin.

Tests cover the mixed-partial and s3-pair-plus-rest-token cases and assert a
cross-origin redirect target receives neither the Authorization header nor the
session token. Also closes a response body left open in an existing test.

subject: perf(table): bound the scan reorder heap at scan concurrency above one (#2039)
body:
* perf(table): add lagging-task reorder heap benchmark and test

BenchmarkArrowScanReorderHeapLaggingTask in
table/arrow_scanner_reorder_bench_test.go scans M single-batch data
files at WithMaxConcurrency(4) with the Open of task 0's file gated
until the other M - 1 files have been read, and reports the peak
HeapInuse delta while the gate is closed and the number of batches the
other files produced in that window. On Apple M3 Pro, 11 cores,
go1.25.9, -count=3, the delta is 4.7 MB at M = 8, 20 to 23 MB at
M = 32 and 96 MB at M = 128, with M - 1 batches held every time.

TestArrowScanReorderHeapBoundedWhileHeadTaskLags in
table/arrow_scanner_reorder_test.go runs the same scan inside a
testing/synctest bubble. synctest.Wait returns once every scan
goroutine is durably blocked, so the count of out-of-order batches the
pipeline holds is read at a fixed point with no sleeps, both before a
fix (all M - 1 other files are read) and after one (workers park on
credits). It asserts the count never exceeds numWorkers x K with K = 2
as reorderCreditsPerWorker. On main it fails with 31 held batches
against a bound of 8, then releases the gate, checks that every row
arrives and checks that the CheckedAllocator is empty.

Refs #2038.

Signed-off-by: KranzL <50032317+KranzL@users.noreply.github.com>

* perf(table): bound the scan reorder heap at scan concurrency above one

Each scan worker in recordBatchesFromTasksAndDeletes and in
makePositionDeleteRecordsForFilter now holds a task credit. The worker
takes the credit before it takes a task, the credit rides on the
task's Last record, and it comes back when the iterator's consumer
takes that record, when the deferred drain loop takes it, or when
MakeSequencedChanWithDiscard discards it at close. A worker waiting
for its credit also waits on the scan context, so cancellation still
stops it. Error records carry no credit.

A worker therefore cannot start its next task while any batch of its
previous task is still in the records channel, the reorder heap or
the sequenced channel. While the head task lags, each other worker
finishes one task and parks, so the heap holds at most numWorkers - 1
tasks instead of every task the free workers can reach. Decoding
inside a task is not throttled and the head task's worker never waits.

Per-batch credits, as #2038 proposed, were measured first on
BenchmarkArrowScanManyFilesAndBatches (32 files of 32 one-row batches,
concurrency 4): K = 2 took 141.6 ms/op against 69.4 ms/op on main,
K = 8 took 127.9 ms/op and K = 32 took 78.7 ms/op, because the batches
a free worker may run ahead are the scan's parallelism. With the
per-task credit that benchmark is within noise of main in interleaved
runs (benchstat, n = 10: +0.4%, -0.2% and +1.5% on the three
sub-benchmarks), and BenchmarkArrowScanReorderHeapLaggingTask holds 3
gated batches and 2.0 to 2.3 MB of peak heap delta for M = 8, 32 and
128, where main holds M - 1 batches and 4.7, 20 to 25 and 95 MB.

The doc on WithCompactionArrowBatchSize now states the bound that
holds, workers x (rows in the largest task + n) +
(recordBatchBufferSize + 2) x n rows, and WithCompactionScanConcurrency
says its worker count multiplies the read-side term.

TestArrowScanReorderHeapBoundedWhileHeadTaskLags asserts the bound of
(numWorkers - 1) x maxInFlightTasksPerWorker completed out-of-order
tasks. TestArrowScanReorderCancelWhileWorkersWaitForTaskCredits
cancels the scan while the free workers are parked and checks that the
iterator returns context.Canceled, every scan goroutine exits and every
batch is released.

Fixes #2038.

Signed-off-by: KranzL <50032317+KranzL@users.noreply.github.com>

* perf(table): hand the scan credit to exactly one record and test the compaction bound

recordSink now tracks whether its worker holds a credit and hands it to
exactly one record: the task's Last record in send, or the error record
in fail when no Last record was sent. processRecords can send Last and
then return an error from the reader or the deferred close, so fail
hands off nil in that case. No path abandons a credit any more, and a
worker that failed and went back to reserve would wait only until its
error record leaves the sequenced channel. The three delete-loader
error sites in recordBatchesFromTasksAndDeletes go through sink.fail,
so fail is the only path that puts an error record into records.
recordSink is a pointer built only by newRecordSink, so a nil sink
panics on first use instead of hanging on a nil channel send. The nil
guard in acquire is gone; taskCredits is declared before
enumeratedRecord.

Scan.ReadTasks now states the bound for the general scan: each worker
holds the decoded batches of at most one task until the iterator has
returned them, so the batches waiting behind a slow early task total at
most the worker count times the rows in the largest task, rounded up to
a multiple of the batch size, and one large file among small ones still
holds its whole decoded contents while it waits. ToArrowRecords and
WithMaxConcurrency point at that paragraph.

TestRecordSinkHandsOffCreditOnce covers fail without Last, Last followed
by fail, and that reserve blocks while the credit is out.
TestExecuteCompactionGroupRecordPipelineBounded drives
ExecuteCompactionGroup with four scan workers and a writer queue of two
over 32 single-batch files inside testing/synctest, gating task 0 in
Open and then the output file in Create, and checks 3 fully read tasks
while task 0 is gated and exactly 8 while the writer is gated, the two
terms of the bound on WithCompactionArrowBatchSize counted in tasks.
With the credit gate disabled the counts are 31 and 32.

Signed-off-by: KranzL <50032317+KranzL@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(table): write uncompressed parquet in the synctest compaction fixture

TestExecuteCompactionGroupRecordPipelineBounded wrote zstd parquet
inside its synctest bubble. arrow-go keeps zstd encoders in a global
sync.Pool and klauspost's Encoder creates its encoders channel on first
use, so the first zstd write inside the bubble left a pooled encoder
whose channel belongs to the bubble. When a later test reused that
encoder, go1.25.9 failed the whole package with "receive on synctest
channel from outside bubble" (seen in TestClusteredWriter on the
ubuntu and macos go1.25.9 jobs; go1.26.1 passes). Locally the pool was
usually cleared by GC before the next zstd write, which is why the
suite passed here; with GOGC=off it fails every time.

The reorder fixture now sets write.parquet.compression-codec to
uncompressed, so no codec pool is touched inside the bubble. With
GOGC=off the pair TestExecuteCompactionGroupRecordPipelineBounded and
TestClusteredWriter passes three times in a row.

subject: fix(table): convert int-backed decimal row group bounds (#2009)
body:
Parquet plain-encodes INT32/INT64-backed decimal statistics little-endian,
while an Iceberg bound is big-endian two's complement. TestRowGroup stored
the stat bytes as bounds unchanged, so they decoded to unrelated values and
pruned row groups that do match, silently dropping rows from scan results.

Reverse the stat bytes for those two physical types before storing them,
in a parquetStatsBounds helper that any evaluator populating bounds from
Parquet statistics should go through. FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY-backed decimals
are already big-endian in Parquet and pass through untouched. The reversed
4- or 8-byte bounds are wider than the spec's minimum width, but they are
only used in memory and UnmarshalBinary is width-tolerant, so they decode
as-is. arrow-go plain-encodes little-endian on big-endian hosts too, so the
conversion does not depend on the host architecture.

Closes #1876

subject: fix(catalog/sql): widen the write-retry budget for lock contention (#2036)
body:
* fix(catalog/sql): widen the write-retry budget for lock contention

Concurrent CreateTable/CreateView against a SQLite catalog could fail with
SQLITE_BUSY instead of ErrTableAlreadyExists/ErrViewAlreadyExists.

SQLite serializes writers, and the write transaction in these paths reads
(namespace existence, identifier availability) before it inserts. A lock
conflict on that upgrade is reported immediately and does not consult the busy
handler, so a busy timeout cannot absorb it -- only retrying the whole
transaction can, which retrySerializableWriteTx already does. The budget was
just too small: 3 attempts with 10ms/20ms backoff is 30ms of waiting, and a
loaded machine holds the write lock longer than that. When the budget ran out
before the winning transaction committed, the losing caller saw the driver's
lock error rather than the catalog conflict it should report.

Raise the budget to 6 attempts (~310ms). It costs nothing without contention,
since the delays only apply between failed attempts.

This was observed as a flaky TestConcurrentTableViewCollisionReturnsCatalogSentinel,
which failed on main and on unrelated pull requests.

The new regression test makes the contention deterministic by holding the
database write lock for longer than the old budget; it fails before this change
and passes after.

Signed-off-by: Matt Topol <zotthewizard@gmail.com>

* fix(catalog/sql): tighten contention test margin, document cross-dialect budget

others get fresh IDs from nextID. This lets callers evolve a table
schema declaratively without reusing retired column IDs, by passing the
current schema as base and counting up from last-column-id.

subject: fix(table): stop MetadataBuilder.Build from growing the metadata log (#2095)
body:
* fix(table): stop MetadataBuilder.Build from growing the metadata log

buildCommonMetadata appended the previous metadata file to b.metadataLog
and trimmed it in place, so every Build() on a builder with changes left
one more identical entry behind. Transactions call Build() several times
before committing: a copy-on-write delete builds once per rewritten file,
and StagedTable() and Transaction.Scan build again. A staged table after a

Out-of-scope categories 4 (malicious catalog) and 5 (equivalent-harm)
omitted the availability-boundary trigger that the section header and the
in-scope preamble both apply to every default. A malicious control plane
pushing Iceberg Go past the documented Puffin blob-size limit therefore

reviewable. All eight categories now carry the trigger.

  its reassess conditions, matching Boundary 1.
- The Scanner Calibration closer now says "Iceberg Go-owned shared state
  crossing separately constructed catalog or client instances" rather than
  the unqualified "shared state", preserving the caller-owned carve-out

subject: refactor(internal): move test mocks to internal/iomock (#2080)
body:
refactor(internal): move test mocks to internal/iomock, unlink testify from the library

MockFS, MockFSReadFile and MockFile lived in internal/mock_fs.go, a non-test
file in package internal that imports github.com/stretchr/testify/mock. Because
the root iceberg package imports internal, every consumer that used iceberg-go
only for its types linked testify (and its objx and yaml deps) into their
production binary.

Move the mocks to a dedicated internal/iomock package that only _test.go files
import. The root iceberg package's dependency closure loses testify, objx and
go.yaml.in/yaml/v3: for a types-only consumer that is 7 fewer packages and 3
fewer modules, with no test framework linked into production. testify remains a
test dependency of the module.

No production code referenced these mocks; only test files did, and they now
import internal/iomock.
